content: When this product is expired or no longer needed, it should be discarded properly. The information provided here was last updated in September 2024. Important Note on Usage of This Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Uses of the Medication: This medication is prescribed to manage symptoms of a specific bowel disease known as ulcerative colitis. It works by reducing inflammation and swelling in the affected area. Budesonide belongs to a class of drugs called corticosteroids. While it does not cure ulcerative colitis, it can help alleviate symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, and bloody stools. How to Use the Medication: Before starting budesonide, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Review it again each time you receive a refill. Follow the illustrated instructions for proper application. This medication is typically administered as a foam into the rectum, as directed by your doctor. The usual regimen involves applying it in the morning and evening for the first two weeks, followed by once daily in the evening for the next four weeks. This medication is flammable. Avoid smoking while applying it and immediately afterward. It is best to use this medication after a bowel movement. You may apply it while standing, lying down, or sitting. Do not insert any part of the canister directly into the anus. Use the enclosed applicator for application. Follow the instructions for attaching the applicator to the canister. Warm the canister in your hands and shake it well for 10 to 15 seconds before use. Hold the canister upside down, gently insert the applicator tip into the anus, and press down on the pump. Hold the pump in position for two seconds to release the foam. Afterward, release your finger from the pump and keep the applicator in place for 10 to 15 seconds. Remove the applicator and dispose of it properly. Wash your hands thoroughly after use. If you are taking another corticosteroid orally (e.g., prednisone), do not stop taking it unless instructed by your doctor. Abruptly stopping corticosteroids can worsen certain conditions, such as asthma or allergies, and may lead to withdrawal symptoms like weakness, weight loss, nausea, muscle pain, headache, fatigue, or dizziness. To prevent withdrawal, your doctor may gradually reduce the dose of your previous medication after starting budesonide. Notify your doctor or pharmacist immediately if you experience withdrawal symptoms. Use this medication consistently to achieve the best results. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day. Do not increase your dose, use it more frequently, or continue using it longer than prescribed. Do not stop using this medication without consulting your doctor, as some conditions may worsen if the drug is suddenly discontinued. Side Effects: Nausea may occur as a side effect. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may be absorbed into the bloodstream, potentially causing side effects associated with excessive corticosteroid levels. These effects are more likely in children and individuals using the medication for an extended period. This medication may weaken your immune system, increasing your susceptibility to serious (and rarely fatal) infections or worsening existing infections. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Precautions: Before using budesonide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Prolonged use of corticosteroids may impair your body’s ability to respond to physical stress. Budesonide may mask signs of infection, making you more susceptible to new infections or worsening existing ones. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using budesonide before receiving any vaccinations. Although unlikely, prolonged use of this medication may temporarily slow a child’s growth. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Babies born to mothers who have used corticosteroids for an extended period may develop hormone-related issues. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke (typically 81-162 milligrams daily), continue taking it unless instructed otherwise. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lifestyle Recommendations: To reduce the risk of bone loss (osteoporosis) during long-term corticosteroid treatment, consider weight-bearing exercises, ensuring adequate calcium and vitamin D intake, quitting smoking, and limiting alcohol consumption. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from heat and open flames, as it is flammable. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024.
